s1.title: Before Pregnancy – Normal Signs
s1.i3: No serious illness or controlled conditions
s1.i5: Good hemoglobin level (12–16 g/dL for women)
s1.i7: Start taking folic acid before conception

s3.title: During Pregnancy – Normal Signs
s3.i7: Mild back pain and leg cramps

s4.title: During Pregnancy – Abnormal Signs
s4.i1: Heavy vaginal bleeding at any stage
s4.i4: Severe headache, blurred vision, or flashes
s4.i5: Sudden swelling in face, hands, or feet
s4.i6: Reduced or no baby movement after 28 weeks
s4.i10: Symptoms of gestational diabetes or preeclampsia

s5.title: After Delivery – Normal Signs (Mother)
s5.i1: Lochia (vaginal discharge) for 4–6 weeks, gradually reducing
s5.i3: Breast engorgement when milk comes in (day 2–5)
s5.i5: Mild baby blues for up to 2 weeks
s5.i7: Tenderness for a few weeks after cesarean

s6.title: After Delivery – Abnormal Signs (Mother)
s6.i1: Heavy bleeding soaking more than one pad per hour
s6.i4: Postpartum depression signs lasting over 2 weeks
s6.i5: Redness, swelling, or pus at cesarean wound
s6.i6: Painful, red, swollen area in breast (mastitis)
s6.i7: Chest pain or difficulty breathing (blood clots)
s6.i8: Severe headache or vision changes (postpartum preeclampsia)
s6.i9: Unable to urinate or severe pain while urinating

s7.title: Newborn – Normal Signs
s7.i7: Up to 10% birth weight loss in first week, normalizes by day 10–14
s7.i9: Soft spots on head (fontanelle) are normal
s7.i10: Umbilical cord falls off in 1–3 weeks

s8.title: Newborn – Abnormal Signs
s8.i1: No crying or very weak cry at birth
s8.i2: Blue lips or central cyanosis (heart/lung problem)
s8.i4: Deep yellow color spreading to limbs

s9.title: Month 1 & 2 – First Trimester Diet
s9.i1: Folic acid rich foods: spinach, broccoli, lentils, fortified cereals
s9.i2: Vitamin B6 foods for nausea: ginger tea, crackers, banana
s9.i3: Small frequent meals to manage morning sickness
s9.i4: Citrus fruits for Vitamin C (oranges, lemon water)
s9.i5: Whole grains for energy: oats, brown rice

s10.title: Month 3 & 4 – Early Second Trimester Diet
s10.i1: Iron rich foods: red meat, chicken, fish, beans, tofu
s10.i2: Calcium sources: milk, yogurt, paneer, cheese
s10.i3: Vitamin D: eggs, fortified milk, sunlight
s10.i4: Magnesium: nuts, seeds, dark chocolate, avocado
s10.i5: Increase protein: 2–3 protein servings per day
s10.i6: Hydration: 8–10 glasses of water per day
s10.i7: Healthy fats: walnuts, flaxseeds, olive oil

s11.title: Month 5 & 6 – Mid Second Trimester Diet
s11.i1: Omega-3 fatty acids: salmon, sardines, chia seeds (brain development)
s11.i2: Fiber rich foods for constipation: fruits, vegetables, whole grains
s11.i3: Iron + Vitamin C: spinach and lemon juice
s11.i5: Potassium: banana, sweet potato (reduce leg cramps)
s11.i6: Continue calcium and Vitamin D supplements
s11.i7: Avoid processed and high-sodium junk food

s12.title: Month 7 & 8 – Third Trimester Diet
s12.i1: High calorie nutritious foods: nuts, seeds, nut butter
s12.i2: Continue iron supplements – daily iron rich foods
s12.i3: Vitamin K: leafy greens (kale, spinach) for blood clotting
s12.i4: Choline: eggs, chicken liver (baby brain health)
s12.i5: Small meals every 2–3 hours to avoid heartburn
s12.i6: Avoid gas-producing foods: cabbage, excess beans
s12.i7: 6 dates daily from week 36 may ease delivery

s13.title: Month 9 – Final Month Diet
s13.i1: Light, easily digestible meals as baby presses on stomach
s13.i2: Coconut water for hydration and electrolytes
s13.i3: Raspberry leaf tea (ask doctor) – may support uterus
s13.i4: Continue iron, calcium, and folic acid supplements
s13.i5: Avoid spicy, oily, and heavy foods
s13.i6: High fiber diet to prevent constipation before delivery
s13.i7: Stay well hydrated – at least 10 glasses of water
s13.i8: Small portions every 2 hours to avoid bloating
